summary: The article accurately describes the quarterly review process and the current interest rates for small savings schemes in India, aligning with official announcements and financial news reports.

claims.claim: The Indian government reviews interest rates for popular small savings schemes like PPF every three months.
claims.note: The Ministry of Finance reviews and announces these rates quarterly.

claims.claim: The next announcement, setting rates for July-September 2026 (Q2 FY27), is expected by the end of June.
claims.note: Rates are reviewed and announced quarterly, typically at the end of March, June, September, and December, for the subsequent quarter.

claims.claim: The Ministry of Finance, specifically its Department of Economic Affairs, is responsible for setting the interest rates for these 12 small savings schemes.
claims.note: The Ministry of Finance, Government of India, determines the interest rates on all small savings schemes.

claims.claim: These interest rates are generally linked to the yields of government securities (G-secs) of similar maturity.
claims.note: The interest rates on small savings schemes are linked to the yields of government securities (G-Secs) of comparable maturities.

claims.claim: As of the current April-June 2026 quarter, some of the interest rates are, for example: Public Provident Fund (PPF) at 7.1%, Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS) at 8.2%, Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana at 8.2%, and National Savings Certificates (NSC) at 7.7%.
claims.note: For the April-June 2026 quarter, PPF is 7.1%, SCSS is 8.2%, Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana is 8.2%, and NSC is 7.7%.

claims.claim: The interest your PPF account earns each financial year depends on the rate declared for that specific quarter.
claims.note: Investors already holding PPF accounts earn the prevailing rate, which the government can change each quarter.

claims.claim: While the RBI's policies on overall interest rates (like the repo rate) influence the market, it is the Ministry of Finance that officially announces the interest rates for small savings schemes.
claims.note: The Ministry of Finance, Government of India, determines the interest rates on all small savings schemes.

article_title: What's Happening with Your PPF and Other Small Savings Rates?
